profile.headline: Founding Software Engineer, Agency Robotics | Building the Engine for Retail Logistics
profile.summary:
At Agency Robotics, we're on a mission to optimize the movement of goods and make supply chains more human-friendly.

Modern commerce is running on legacy infrastructure—expensive, inflexible, and built for bulk—while customers increasingly expect faster, more flexible, and more personalized service. We build simple, flexible, and intelligent sortation systems to help 3PLs, retailers, and parcel carriers power their operations and meet changing customer demands.

Personally, I’m a software engineer and technical leader with over 20 years of experience in simulation, robotics, and distributed systems. I’ve consistently driven measurable improvements in performance and cost across a wide range of projects. I thrive both in leading high-performing teams and contributing directly to solving complex, meaningful challenges.

positions.title: Founding Software Engineer
positions.description: Agency Robotics builds robotic sortation infrastructure to power 3PLs, retailers and parcel carriers.

positions.title: Lead Software Engineer
positions.description:
Principal Engineer and Squad Lead. Led a team of twelve first in charge of robot simulation and then across allocation, containerization, waypoint sorting, and order induction.

Developed a high-fidelity robot simulation used across engineering and warehouse teams to test systems and process changes before live deployment. It is now a core part of 6 River’s development lifecycle.

Despite being new to the stack, I built a web-based warehouse viewer using Node.js, TypeScript, Angular, RxJS, Docker, and Kubernetes. It enables real-time monitoring for both customers and internal teams, and acts as a GUI for the simulation, including tools to edit live warehouse maps.

Expanded the simulation with a custom scripting environment to support QA and debugging. This became the foundation for our automated integration and stress tests, saving hundreds of hours by catching issues before live deployment.

Identified inefficiencies in our job allocation logic and overhauled the algorithm—leading to my ownership of the entire allocation system. Improvements included real-time warehouse state tracking, predictive analysis, and dynamic priority management based on human behavior. These changes increased overall system performance by over 30%, saving millions.

Led efforts to scale the system, drastically reducing CPU and memory usage and increasing capacity 40×—unlocking access to larger customers. Following this success, I was placed in charge the team responsible for of our full allocation stack.

After Ocado’s acquisition of 6 River Systems, I was among the few engineers retained from a 90% layoff due to my key role. In my expanded position, I became the sole engineer responsible for allocation and containerization. Despite reduced resources, I delivered new features, maintained uptime, and drove further improvements, boosting allocation performance another 20%. This system is now viewed as the company’s leading competitive advantage.

positions.title: Director of Link Products
positions.description:
Director of Link Products (2013–2015): Led the company’s most profitable product line. This includes architecture design, product roadmaps, as well as an engineering team across many successful product releases. Designed optimizations to the products, improving speed by nearly 10× allowing for the largest NATO simulations to date.

Senior Solutions Engineer (2012–2013): Bridged engineering and sales, traveling globally to present tech and design high-level simulation systems. Built custom features and plug-ins to serve customer training objectives. 

Software Architect (2010–2012): Lead engineer for AI offerings, B-HAVE and Kynapse. Delivered simulation behavior tools, merging pathfinding and decision-making technologies.

Senior Software Engineer (2007–2010): Recovered a failing Navy contract, years behind schedule, to a successful finish. As a result I created the HLA Traffic Analyzer, a large system that involved the merger of much of MAK’s technology into a comprehensive simulation monitoring tool. 

Principal developer for the VR-Exchange and the MAK Gateway. Both of these are translators that allow protocols and exercises to link together, even if the different components were originally not designed to work with each other.  During my time leading the product, VR-Exchange tripled its yearly sales.

Software Engineer (2000–2006): Principal investigator for a Navy-funded tool (FOMspy) with a custom scripting language and live simulation inspection. As part of this, I created a library that madepossible to view real-time simulation data in human readable form. This library allowed for a code generation feature that is now a centerpiece of VR-Link, MAK’s best selling product. It was also used for the MAK Logger and the MAK RTI for the real time analysis features that have become critical for the success of these products.

Developed the MAK PVD, an advanced 2-D battlefield display that was the basis for the front-end of VR-Forces, MAK's flagship product.
